closest_prior_work.citation: Brown, C. F., et al. (2025). AlphaEarth Foundations: An embedding field model for accurate and efficient global mapping from sparse label data. arXiv:2507.22291.
closest_prior_work.difference: Establishes broad sparse-label embedding performance, described as extrapolating annotations to Earth-observation archives, but does not test patch-first training allocation or small-patch recovery.

closest_prior_work.citation: Ryan, S., Powell, M., Ling, J., & Wen, L. (2026). Streamlining Wetland Vegetation Mapping with AlphaEarth Embeddings. Remote Sensing, 18, 293.
closest_prior_work.difference: Compares AlphaEarth with traditional multisensor wetland-vegetation workflows, but does not use matched fitting positions to isolate allocation-by-representation effects on individual small patches.

closest_prior_work.citation: Corcoran, J., Knight, J., Pelletier, K., Rampi, L., & Wang, Y. (2015). The Effects of Point or Polygon Based Training Data on RandomForest Classification Accuracy of Wetlands. Remote Sensing, 7, 4002-4025.
closest_prior_work.difference: Previously compared point, fixed-window and image-object training for wetland RF classification; this paper instead keeps pixel predictors and output grid fixed while changing only fitting-position allocation.

closest_prior_work.citation: Halabisky, M., et al. (2023). The Wetland Intrinsic Potential tool. Hydrology and Earth System Sciences, 27, 3687-3699.
closest_prior_work.difference: Already stratified training points by preliminary wetland-probability classes, including uncertain areas; this paper tests whether image-derived proposals or uncertainty can reproduce an inventory-oracle patch-first benefit.

closest_prior_work.citation: Zhou, P., et al. (2025). Using an Area-Weighted Loss Function to Address Class Imbalance in Deep Learning-Based Mapping of Small Water Bodies. Remote Sensing, 17, 1868.
closest_prior_work.difference: Already proposed dynamically size-weighting water bodies during training; this paper uses reciprocal-size weighting only as a diagnostic for fixed RF representations and wetland patches.

main_issues.issue: The headline 11.6 pp interaction uses thresholds standardized on pooled test-reference uplands, so it is not a deployable operating-point effect; the validation-threshold replay interaction is 4.5 pp with interval including zero, and transferred thresholds give a negative pooled embedding gain.

The planned split is the most favourable of four: three exploratory rotations give interactions of 4.7, -0.4 and 1.2 pp with intervals including zero, while pooled rotation evidence attenuates the interaction to 4.5 pp and shows optical gains too.

Patch-first allocation is not cleanly isolated: it simultaneously changes patch size, geography, habitat, boundary exposure and sub-minimum-mapping-unit representation; core-matching and inverse-size weighting show part of the gain is metric-aligned reweighting rather than newly exposed patches.

The equal-patch recovery metric is aligned by construction with patch-first sampling, while average precision falls and pixel producer accuracy/IoU are essentially flat, so the result is a trade-off at one coverage definition rather than a general accuracy improvement.

The representation contrast is confounded: AlphaEarth v2.1 annual multisensor embeddings differ from the seasonal Sentinel-2 construction in information content, effective resolution and pretraining, and possible pretraining overlap with inventory-related labels is not excluded, so no embedding-specific causal interpretation is supported.

Scope is narrow and reference-bound: four convenience US NWI projects, nominally 2020 but with heterogeneous source years and mapping procedures, palustrine classes only, and agreement with an existing inventory rather than ecological wetland presence.

Uncertainty is understated: the primary interval resamples only four test cores per region conditional on fitted models and thresholds, excludes split/training/reference uncertainty, and the many secondary and post-result analyses have no multiplicity control.

From the paper alone exact cores, source-feature IDs, scene lists and code are deferred to external reproduction records, and the dense exploratory reporting plus a cropped validation-replay figure panel impede independent checking and reading.

research_question.predictable_reason: Patch-first sampling by definition upweights small patches when success is weighted equally per patch, so the direction of an oracle gain was partly built in, although the embedding-versus-optical difference and failed geographic transfer were not.
research_question.question: How does patch-first versus area-based allocation of a fixed training-point budget interact with annual satellite embeddings versus seasonal optical predictors in recovering small mapped wetland patches at a common false-positive rate, and can image-derived allocation recover the oracle benefit?

score_reasons.clarity: Key terms are defined, but the abstract and results are overloaded with planned, secondary and exploratory conditions, caveats and appendix sensitivities; one results figure is cropped.
score_reasons.correctness: Internal comparisons are carefully paired and limitations are disclosed, but the main interaction is fragile across splits, relies on a test-standardized threshold, and is not supported as a deployable or transferable effect.
score_reasons.generality: Evidence covers only four heterogeneous US inventory projects, one year, one embedding product, simple decoders and inventory agreement; whole-project transfer and threshold transport fail.
score_reasons.novelty: The exact frozen-embedding, matched-position, small-patch-recovery combination is incremental rather than conceptually new, given prior object/polygon training and object-accuracy work addressing polygon-size sampling issues.
score_reasons.usefulness: Usefully warns practitioners to report patch recovery beside pixel metrics and validate thresholds locally, but the oracle needs an existing inventory and no annotation-cost or conservation benefit is measured.
score_reasons.verifiability: Sampling, classifiers, budgets, patch definitions and deviations are unusually detailed, yet exact core identifiers, scene lists and executable records are external to the paper and the self-check is not independent reproduction.

strengths: Matched fitting positions across representations and shared negative positions make the central allocation contrast unusually well controlled.
The paper transparently separates the planned analysis from post-result exploratory checks and reports unfavourable split-rotation, transfer and threshold-replay results.
Extensive controls cover budgets, decoders, regional quotas, class-count matching, inverse-size weighting, coverage definitions and reference-shift stress tests.
It usefully demonstrates that near-constant pixel accuracy can coexist with materially different small-patch recovery.
review.summary: The paper compares area-based, oracle patch-first and image-derived training-point allocation for AlphaEarth embeddings versus seasonal Sentinel-2 predictors in four US wetland-inventory projects. On the planned split, oracle allocation improves small-patch recovery much more for embeddings than optical predictors, but exploratory pooling over four splits attenuates the interaction, optical predictors also benefit, validation-threshold replay is inconclusive for the interaction, and whole-project threshold transfer fails. The study is exceptionally transparent about these limits, yet its contribution is an incremental, narrow and fragile empirical quantification rather than a robust deployable sampling advantage.
